chunks: From him, from Fadala, from Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Kathir, from his father, who said:

A man asked Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) about the found property (luqatah), so he said: 'Announce it. If its owner comes, hand it over to him; otherwise, keep it for a year. If the owner or someone seeking it does not come, give it in charity. If the owner comes after it has been given in charity, if he wishes, he bears the cost of what was with the giver, and the reward is for the giver; and if he dislikes that, he considers it [as a gift/compensation], and the reward is for the giver.'

key_terms.اغْتَرَمَهَا: To bear the cost/compensate for it
key_terms.اللُّقَطَة: Found property or lost item picked up from the ground

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for handling found property (luqatah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam Ali (AS) via Abu Basir, establishes the procedural framework for 'luqatah' (found property) in Shia fiqh, emphasizing the duty of announcement and the one-year holding period. It uniquely addresses the post-charity reclamation scenario, distinguishing between the finder's financial liability (gharamah) and the preservation of spiritual reward (ajr), reflecting the juristic balance between property rights and charitable merit. This ruling is foundational in the chapter of Luqatah within Al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-Ahkam, illustrating the practical application of justice in transactional ethics.
